intro: A CI trust rule lets a GitHub Actions or GitLab CI job deploy without a stored token: the job exchanges its OIDC ID token for a short-lived token that acts as a service account, for one deploy of its own commit or one dry run. Only the jobs whose ID token has every claim the rule names, exactly, are accepted.
none: No CI trust rule yet. Add one to let a CI job deploy without a stored token.

page.conditions: Claims the ID token must have
page.conditionsHelp: Each claim must be in the ID token and equal this text exactly: no case folding, no trimming.
page.startsJobsYes: starts the project's jobs with on_deploy: true in {{environment}}
page.startsJobsNo: starts no job; each job with on_deploy: true is named in the deploy's warning
page.deployGrant: {{principal}} also needs DEPLOY on {{environment}}: the rule names who CI acts as, the grants decide what it may do.
page.workflowText: lakana init writes the workflow file that exchanges the ID token. Set LAKANA_OIDC in the job, and give it permission to ask for an ID token.
page.workflowGithub: Deploy from GitHub Actions without a stored secret
page.workflowGitlab: Deploy from GitLab CI without a stored secret
page.disableText: No CI job is accepted under it until it is enabled again, and the tokens issued under it end now.
page.enabledNote: Enabled. CI jobs that match are accepted again.
page.disabledNote: Disabled. No CI job is accepted under it.
page.savedNote: Saved. The tokens issued under the rule before have ended.
page.deleteText: CI jobs are no longer accepted under it, and the tokens issued under it end now. To stop it for a while, disable it instead.

dialog.issuerUrlHelp: A self-hosted GitLab, exactly as the server's LAKANA_CI_OIDC__ISSUERS names it.
dialog.environmentHelp: The environment the CI job may deploy to.
dialog.repositoryHelp: The registered repository it may deploy.
dialog.principalHelp: An active service account. It needs its own DEPLOY grant on the environment.
dialog.startsJobs: Start the project's jobs with on_deploy: true after each deploy
dialog.startsJobsHelp: As the rule's account, in this environment only. Off, the deploy succeeds and names each job it did not start.
dialog.conditions: Claims the ID token must have
dialog.conditionsHelpGithub: Pin the repository's number (repository_id), a ref or environment, and how the run was started: event_name or environment.
dialog.conditionsHelpGitlab: Pin the project's number (project_id), a ref or environment, and how the pipeline was started: ref_protected, pipeline_source or environment.
dialog.managed: An access file manages {{environment}}: add this rule to the ci_trust section of {{file}} instead.
dialog.principalNeeded: Fill in the service account it acts as.
dialog.kindsNeeded: Allow deploy, dry run or both.
dialog.conditionsNeeded: Give every claim a name and the text it must equal.
dialog.endsTokens: Saving ends the tokens issued under the rule before.

explain.title: Explain a CI job's claims
explain.intro: Paste the decoded claims of the job's ID token (its payload as JSON, never the token itself) to see which rule an exchange would match, and why the others do not. Nothing is changed or recorded, and no token is issued.
explain.issuerHelp: Leave it empty to compare the claims' iss.
explain.environmentNeeded: Choose the environment the job deploys to.
explain.notJson: The claims are not JSON: paste the ID token's decoded payload, one JSON object.
explain.notObject: The claims must be one JSON object, the ID token's decoded payload.
explain.looksLikeToken: This looks like an ID token, not its claims. Paste only the decoded payload: a token is a credential and is never sent here.
